# `pipeline`: run tools tile by tile {#sec-pipeline}

## What it does

`pipeline` runs a chain of FUSION2 tools across an area too large to
process as one piece. It splits the area into tiles, adds a buffer of
extra points around each tile so that edge cells and edge trees see
their full neighbourhood, runs the chain of tools on each tile in
parallel, trims each result back to its tile, and stitches the tiles
together.

A `groundfilter` stage's ground surface is passed automatically to every
later stage that needs one, so a chain such as
`groundfilter,canopymodel,canopymaxima` goes from raw points to tree tops
in one command. `pipeline` records each tile's progress, so an
interrupted run resumes where it stopped. @sec-many-tiles covers
large-area runs in more depth.

## Example commands

The example splits the example tile into four 100 x 100 ft tiles and
runs ground filtering, canopy height modelling, and tree-top detection
on each.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/pipeline` | `groundfilter,canopymodel,canopymaxima` | The tools to run on each tile, in order. `/tool:<name>` runs a single tool. |
| `/input` | `TC_1372_forest200ft.laz` | A LAS/LAZ file or a folder of them. |
| `/output` | `out/pipeline` | Folder for the stitched results. |
| `/extent` | the tile's bounds | The area to tile, as lower-left X, lower-left Y, upper-right X, upper-right Y. |
| `/tilesize` | `100,100` | Tile width and height, 100 ft. |
| `/buffer` | `20` | Extra points read around each tile, 20 ft. |
| `/cellsize` | `3` | Passed on to every stage that accepts it. |
| `/minht` | `2` | Passed on to every stage that accepts it. |
| `/merge` | | Also merge each raster stage's tiles into one GeoTIFF, besides the virtual raster (`.vrt`). |

: Options used in the `pipeline` example. {#tbl-options-pipeline}

Options that belong to individual tools (`/cellsize`, `/minht`, `/class`,
`/strata`, and others) are forwarded to whichever stages accept them.
@sec-cli-options lists every forwarded option.

## Outputs

- **Per raster stage**: `<stage>.vrt`, a virtual raster joining the
  tiles, and with `/merge` a single `<stage>_merged.tif`
  (`groundfilter_merged.tif`, `canopymodel_merged.tif`).
- **Per table stage**: one combined table (`canopymaxima_all.csv`).
- **`_processing/`**: each tile's intermediate files and log, plus
  `pipeline_state.csv`, which records the status, exit code, and times of
  every tile and stage. This is what lets a run resume.

## Results

@fig-pipeline-maps shows the stitched canopy model with tree tops (left),
and the difference between the stitched and single-run canopy model
(middle) and ground surface (right). Dashed lines mark the tile
boundaries. The stitched map shows no seam along them, the difference
maps are mostly near zero, and trees near a boundary appear once, not
twice.

When the tile size is not a whole multiple of the cell size, as with
100 ft tiles and 3 ft cells, a tile's grid can sit a fraction of a cell
away from the single-run grid. Cells then sample slightly different
spots, and the canopy difference map shows scattered differences at
crown edges in the shifted tiles. Choosing a tile size that is a multiple
of the cell size avoids this.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/pipeline_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-pipeline confirms that all four tiles ran with no failed
stage, that the stitched canopy model sits on the tile and matches the
single-run canopy model within a median of 0.5 ft, and that no tree top
is duplicated across tile seams.
